feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 0 and iteration 1 are the only evidence. Iteration 0 (five sensors at ±0.04 m) scored 136 with max_error about 0.0626 m, around 1 line-loss event per run, and 19 of 20 oval trials ended off track. Iteration 1 (seven sensors at ±0.06 m) cut line loss (oval 1.0 to 0.4, s-bend 1.1 to 0.2) but still ended every trial off track, and the score fell to 86. So the sensor span was not the binding limit. What I had to compensate for in the controller: when the span changed, I scaled the weights to the sensor position (about 33 per metre) and raised kp to keep steering gain near the tested level. For this candidate I am reducing kp to 3.6 and raising kd to 0.6, because a narrower track gives about 1.2x more yaw per unit of PWM difference. If the next race shows max_error still at 0.06 m with completion at 0 and the same line-loss rate, the limit is base_speed (set by me), and I will lower it rather than change geometry. If the race shows line loss returning on the s-bend, the five-sensor span is too narrow for that bend, and the outer sensors should move out again.
requested_changes: If completion stays 0 and max_error stays at 0.06 m with no change in line loss, try wheel_track 0.09 m (with mass 0.6 kg held) to test whether more turn authority is still the limit. Evidence: iteration 1 showed that widening sensor coverage alone did not change max_error (0.0615 to 0.0635 m).

If steering_oscillation rises well above the iteration 0 oval level (about 0.30) with no line loss, move the sensor row forward to y = 0.06 m with the same five sensors and 0.02 m spacing, to give more lookahead at the higher effective yaw gain. Evidence: iteration 0 showed oscillation of 0.30 on the oval and 0.25 on the s-bend.

If line_loss_events returns to about 1 per run on the s-bend with max_error near 0.06 m, use outer sensors at x = ±0.05 m with the same five-sensor count and weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]. Evidence: iteration 0 lost the tape at about ±0.058 m, and iteration 1 cut s-bend line loss from 1.1 to 0.2 when coverage was widened.
